lessons.title: If statements in Python
lessons.learningGoal: Write simple if/else branches that compare values and run different code paths.
lessons.fallbackExplanation: Use if when you want Python to choose between paths. The condition must be a boolean expression. Indent the code that belongs to each branch.

fallbackTask.prompt: Write a function `grade_label(score)` that returns "pass" if score is 60 or higher, otherwise "fail".

lessons.lessonNotes: An if statement checks a condition. If the condition is True, the indented block runs. You can add elif for additional checks and else for a default path. Comparison operators like ==, !=, <, and > return True or False.

lessons.title: For loops over sequences
lessons.learningGoal: Use a for loop to visit each item in a list and accumulate a result.
lessons.fallbackExplanation: for item in items runs the loop body once per element. Keep a variable outside the loop when you need to build up an answer.

fallbackTask.prompt: Write `count_positive(numbers)` that returns how many numbers in the list are greater than zero.

lessons.lessonNotes: A for loop repeats once per item in a sequence. The loop variable takes each value in turn. You often initialize a result before the loop and update it inside the loop body.
lessons.videoTitle: How to Loop over Lists in Python

videoAlternates.title: Python For Loops: The Complete Beginner’s Guide

lessons.title: Looping with range()
lessons.learningGoal: Use range() to repeat an action a fixed number of times without off-by-one errors.
lessons.fallbackExplanation: range(stop) ends before stop, not at stop. That is why range(3) gives 0, 1, 2.

fallbackTask.prompt: Write `sum_first_n(n)` that returns 1 + 2 + ... + n. Return 0 when n is 0.

lessons.lessonNotes: range(n) produces 0 through n-1. range(start, stop) excludes stop. A for loop over range is useful when you need an index or a counted repetition.
lessons.videoTitle: How to Loop over Lists in Python

videoAlternates.title: Python Tutorial: Ranged Loops (for i in range)

lessons.title: While loops
lessons.learningGoal: Write a while loop that stops when a condition becomes false and avoid infinite loops.
lessons.fallbackExplanation: Check that the loop condition can become False. Update the variables the condition depends on inside the loop.

fallbackTask.prompt: Write `halve_until_one(n)` that repeatedly integer-divides n by 2 until n is 1 or less, and returns the number of divisions performed. If n is already 1 or less, return 0.

lessons.lessonNotes: A while loop runs while its condition is True. Something inside the loop must eventually make the condition False, or the loop never ends.

For Loop and While Loop in Python Explained

lessons.title: Defining functions
lessons.learningGoal: Define a function with parameters and return a value using return.
lessons.fallbackExplanation: Use return when the caller needs a result. The function body can use its parameters like local variables.

fallbackTask.prompt: Write `rectangle_area(width, height)` that returns the area of a rectangle.

lessons.lessonNotes: def names a function. Parameters are inputs. return sends a value back to the caller. Without return, a function gives back None.

videoAlternates.title: Defining a Function in Python | Python Tutorial for Beginners

lessons.title: Lists and indexing
lessons.learningGoal: Access list elements by index, including negative indices, and return the correct item.
lessons.fallbackExplanation: Valid indices run from 0 to len(items)-1. Index -1 is the last element.

fallbackTask.prompt: Write `first_and_last(items)` that returns a tuple (first, last). Assume items is non-empty.

lessons.lessonNotes: Lists are ordered collections. Index 0 is the first item. Negative indices count from the end. len(list) gives the length.

lessons.title: Building lists
lessons.learningGoal: Build a new list from an existing list using a loop and append.
lessons.fallbackExplanation: result = [] then result.append(x) inside a loop is a common pattern for collecting values.

fallbackTask.prompt: Write `double_evens(numbers)` that returns a new list containing double each even number from numbers (odds are skipped).

lessons.lessonNotes: Start with an empty list. Loop over a source list, transform or filter each item, and append to the result when appropriate.

lessons.title: Functions that use lists
lessons.learningGoal: Combine functions and list iteration to compute an aggregate without mutating the input list.
lessons.fallbackExplanation: Treat the input list as read-only unless asked to modify it. Use a local variable for your running total or result.

fallbackTask.prompt: Write `max_of_three(a, b, c)` that returns the largest of the three numbers.

lessons.lessonNotes: Pass a list into a function as a parameter. Loop over it to compute a summary value. Return the result without changing the original list unless the task requires it.
